samples.sample_label: 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible, then re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold to obtain steel strips of 60×70×2.5 mm by near-rapid solidification.
Aging treatment of a portion of the near-rapid-solidified steel strips in a tubular vacuum furnace at 823 K for 3 h.

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase microstructure of austenite (γ) matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite islands randomly dispersed; submicron NbC particles and intragranular nano-scale κ-carbides present in the austenite.

phases_present.grain_size: ≈9 μm (nearly unchanged after 823 K/3 h aging)

phases_present.morphology: irregular-shaped / vermicular islands dispersed in the austenite matrix
phases_present.grain_size: 3.1 μm (as-cast 0.04Nb value; similar across aging states)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Austenite grain size ≈9 μm (0.04Nb as-cast, nearly unchanged after 823 K/3 h); ferrite grain size 3.1 μm (0.04Nb as-cast).

precipitates.distribution: Dispersed in the austenite matrix (submicron white particles); volume fraction between 1.2 and 1.8 vol% at 823 K/3 h (read from Figure 4).
Intragranular, dispersed in austenite; volume fraction 26.7 vol% after aging at 823 K.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: NbC particles pin austenite grain boundaries, refining austenite grain size (0.04Nb austenite ~9 μm vs 0.02Nb ~18 μm).

interfaces.slip_behavior: Nano-scale κ-carbides are sheared by dislocations during plastic deformation (particle-shearing precipitation strengthening).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging at 823 K/3 h increases intragranular κ-carbide volume fraction (1.6→26.7 vol%) and average size (1.9→6.4 nm) in the 0.04Nb steel; no coarsened intergranular κ-carbides observed after 723–823 K aging.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS Criterion 44 universal testing machine; minimum of four repetitions per strip

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve for 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h reaches the highest stress and terminates at the smallest strain (between 0 and 10% strain).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness tester MH-5L, indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength (0.04Nb steels exceed 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure consists of ferrite and austenite; after aging at 823 K/3 h the diffraction peak intensity of austenite and ferrite shows almost no significant change.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apollo 300 thermal field emission SEM with EBSD detector; Channel 5 software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD step size 300 nm; grain boundaries identified by minimum misorientation angle 15°; samples electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol at 25 V for 10 s
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure characterization, ferrite content, grain size measurement
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed in austenite matrix; 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h has ferrite content 18.1 vol%; austenite grain size ≈9 μm (nearly unchanged after 823 K/3 h aging); ferrite grain size 3.1 μm (as-cast 0.04Nb).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JEM-2100 TEM operating at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM specimens prepared by double-jet electropolishing (10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol) at ~30 °C and 35 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: White submicron particles identified as NbC; intragranular κ-carbides coherent with austenite ([100]γ//[100]κ); at 823 K/3 h κ-carbide average size 6.4 nm and volume fraction 26.7 vol%.
Nb element is uniformly dispersed within the austenite grain, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries in the 0.04Nb steel.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h has average microhardness 477 HV.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature, strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1, gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h: yield strength 1056 ± 28 MPa, tensile strength 1133 ± 33 MPa, total elongation 7 ± 1%.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Explains the similar constituent phase contents in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels and the formation of NbC (MC) particles.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: PAW potentials; U = 2.59 eV for Fe; plane-wave kinetic energy cutoff 500 eV; Gaussian smearing 0.05 eV
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 2×2×2 supercell κ-carbide (Fe3AlC, E21); vacuum spacing 15 Å; 6×6×6 Monkhorst–Pack k-point sampling

analytical_models.model_note: Nb doping significantly increases the κ-carbide formation energy.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Temperature range 673–873 K; diffusion of Al and C in austenite for 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels
Austenite dominant (>80 vol%); parameters M=3.06, α=0.23, b=0.26 nm, G=70 GPa, kγ=14.55 MPa·mm^-1/2, N=6, γ_APB=350 mJ/m^-2; ferrite M_F=2, α_F=0.4, G_F=76 GPa
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated strengthening contributions are compared against the measured yield strength trend.

analytical_models.model_name: Strengthening contributions in austenite (823 K/3 h)
analytical_models.model_note: Values for 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h from Table 9.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 0.04Nb steel strip (wt%): Mn 12.82, Al 9.12, Cr 2.99, C 1.40, Nb 0.039, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
Measured austenite matrix composition of the 0.04Nb steel (wt%): Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038, Fe 64.07 (Table 4).
For the 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h, yield strength rises from 896 MPa (as-cast) to 1056 MPa, while total elongation decreases from 37% to 7%.
The 0.04Nb steels show yield strength ≈71 MPa higher than the 0.02Nb steels, mainly due to additional fine grain strengthening and dislocation strengthening.
No coarsened intergranular κ-carbides were detected in either the 0.02Nb or 0.04Nb steels after aging treatment at 723–823 K.
